title: Guide - Finding Rest - Praying the Psalms

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Finding Rest. <short pause> This practice is called Praying the Psalms. <short pause> If you have no words left at the end of the day, that's all right. <short pause> Tonight, we can borrow some.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Get comfortable, in whatever way is kindest to your body. <short pause> Let your breath come and go. <short pause> You don't need to sound faithful, or feel peaceful, before you pray. <short pause> You can come exactly as tired as you are.

The Psalms are prayers that people have shared for thousands of years. <short pause> They are full of thanks and tears, questions and songs. <short pause> When our own words run out, we can step inside theirs, and find that there is room for us.

Psalm four is a prayer for evening. <short pause> The one praying it has known distress. <short pause> People around them are asking, who will show us any good? <short pause> And still, the prayer ends in bed, with these words from verse eight.
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: We are going to pray that verse one small piece at a time... <short pause> the way you might hold a smooth stone, and turn it over slowly in your hand. <short pause> I'll say a piece, and you can repeat it silently. <short pause> Then we'll make it your own.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: I will both lay me down... <short pause> I will both lay me down. <short pause> Lord, here is my body. <short pause> My heavy legs, my aching back, my busy hands. <short pause> I have carried myself all day. <short pause> Now I lay myself down before You.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: In peace... <short pause> in peace. <short pause> Lord, not everything around me is settled. <short pause> You know the conversation that still hurts, and the answer I am still waiting for. <short pause> I don't have to fix them in order to receive Your peace. <short pause> Meet me in the middle of them.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: And sleep... <short pause> and sleep. <short pause> Lord, I can't make myself sleep. <short pause> I can only stop, and let it come. <short pause> So I loosen my hold on this night. <short pause> Whether sleep comes quickly or slowly, I am resting with You.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: For thou, Lord, only... <short pause> thou, Lord, only. <short pause> Not my planning. <short pause> Not my watching, or my worrying, or getting everything right. <short pause> You alone are God, and I am glad that I am not.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Makest me dwell in safety... <short pause> dwell in safety. <short pause> Lord, let me live inside Your care, and not just visit it. <short pause> Be near to this room, and to the people I love who are sleeping somewhere else tonight. <short pause> I trust them to You as well.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Now hear the whole verse again, as your own prayer. <short pause> Let each word rest where it lands. <short pause> I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.

Lord, <short pause> thank You for giving me words when I had none. <short pause> Hear what I said, and what I didn't know how to say. <short pause> Let Your word be the last voice I listen to today. <short pause> Amen.

If you are awake a little longer, choose the piece that felt most like yours. <short pause> Perhaps it is only two words... <short pause> in peace. <short pause> Say it slowly, as often as you like. <short pause> You don't have to reach the end of it. <short pause> Goodnight.
